summary: Verified the RawPayloadCaptureInterceptor + EbmsMessageProvider raw-XML capture fix in /app/ebms-adapter/ebms-orchestrator. Compiled the module cleanly (mvn -pl ebms-orchestrator -am compile → BUILD SUCCESS). Wrote 4 focused JUnit 5 tests in RawPayloadCaptureInterceptorTest covering: (1) Interceptor captures raw bytes onto the CXF Exchange AND replaces the InputStream with a fresh re-readable copy (proves no 'stream already consumed' downstream SAAJ break). (2) A property put on Exchange by the interceptor IS visible via jakarta.xml.ws.handler.MessageContext.get() as consumed by JAX-WS Provider — via CXF 4.1.8's WrappedMessageContext (bytecode-verified: WrappedMessageContext.get() first checks the wrapped Message map and, on miss with non-null Exchange, delegates to Exchange.get(mapKey(key)); the custom key 'ebms.raw.xml.payload' is not in the jaxws2cxf translation map so it passes through unchanged). (3) Null/absent InputStream is handled without exception. (4) Whitespace/formatting bytes are preserved byte-identically (the exact XML-DSig-digest concern). Result: Tests run: 4, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 in 0.589 s. The fix is architecturally correct: Exchange→WebServiceContext propagation IS real in CXF 4.1.8, and the byte-preservation contract of CachedOutputStream holds. Ping/ACK regression is trivially guaranteed by code inspection (EbmsMessageProvider.invoke lines 63-74 return before line 77 which is the only site that calls extractRawXmlPayload).

minor.issue: Currently rethrows any capture failure as org.apache.cxf.interceptor.Fault, which will 500 the entire inbound request even if the raw-capture is only advisory (the Provider does have a soapToString() fallback). Consider swallowing the exception (log WARN, skip the put) so that a rare capture edge case cannot take down inbound processing that the fallback path could still handle. Not blocking — behavior is defensive but strictly stricter than the fallback.

Stores the raw payload as a heap String. For very large inbound ebMS2 payloads (attachments, large business documents) this doubles the memory footprint (CachedOutputStream + String) for the lifetime of the exchange. Consider storing the CachedOutputStream itself and letting consumers pull the string lazily; or gate capture on a size threshold.

Assumes UTF-8. Per SOAP 1.1 spec this is the norm but the HTTP Content-Type charset parameter can override. If a partner ever POSTs UTF-16 or ISO-8859-1, IOUtils.toString(..., 'UTF-8') will mojibake the payload and break signature verification anyway. Consider reading the charset from message.get(Message.CONTENT_TYPE) or Message.ENCODING.

The private method is not directly unit-tested (only through the interceptor+WrappedMessageContext pair). A tiny Mockito-based test injecting a WebServiceContext with a stubbed MessageContext would seal the coverage. Not a defect.

action_items: OPTIONAL (hardening, not a bug): make handleMessage() swallow-and-log instead of throwing Fault, since the Provider already has a soapToString() fallback — currently a capture failure would 500 the request rather than degrade gracefully.
OPTIONAL: respect the HTTP Content-Type charset parameter instead of hardcoding UTF-8 when converting the captured bytes to a String.

OPTIONAL: extend InboundPipelineIntegrationTest with a real HTTP POST through a random-port SpringBootTest to verify the full CXFServlet→interceptor→SAAJ→Provider chain end-to-end with a signed osb-*-s envelope. Not required for correctness (unit + bytecode analysis already prove the CXF propagation contract) but would guard against future CXF-version regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: RawPayloadCaptureInterceptor correctly registers at Phase.RECEIVE (earliest inbound phase, before SAAJ transport/parsing). This is the right phase for CXF 4.1.8.

CxfEndpointConfig.ebmsEndpoint() uses endpoint.getInInterceptors().add(...) which IS the valid API for org.apache.cxf.jaxws.EndpointImpl in CXF 4.1.8 — it exposes a mutable List<Interceptor<? extends Message>> inherited from AbstractEndpointFactory-published bus, and the interceptor is safely added before publish() so it is picked up on the first inbound message.

Exchange→WebServiceContext visibility CONFIRMED (bytecode-verified against cxf-rt-frontend-jaxws-4.1.8.jar): WrappedMessageContext.get() delegates to Exchange.get() on a Message-map miss. Custom keys like 'ebms.raw.xml.payload' are not in the jaxws→cxf key rename map so they pass through mapKey() unchanged.

InputStream replacement via cos.getInputStream() is correct — CachedOutputStream.getInputStream() returns a fresh, independent InputStream (not one that shares state with a previously-drained source), so downstream SAAJ parsing succeeds normally.

Byte-identity of the captured payload IS preserved (test 4 verifies whitespace/newlines/indentation survive round-trip). This is exactly what XML-DSig Exclusive-C14N needs to compute a digest that matches what the sender canonicalized.

Ping/ACK regression risk is nil: EbmsMessageProvider.invoke() returns at lines 66 (Ping) and 73 (ACK) before ever reaching the extractRawXmlPayload() call at line 77. Interceptor still runs (unavoidable) but only ~1 extra byte-copy and a String allocation per Ping/ACK — negligible.

rca of the issue: Root cause: SoapHelper.soapToString(request) calls SOAPMessage.writeTo(baos) on the already-SAAJ-parsed jakarta.xml.soap.SOAPMessage. SAAJ's serialization is NOT guaranteed to be byte-identical to the input bytes — namespace declarations may be re-emitted, whitespace between elements may be normalized, attribute ordering may change, and MIME framing (in multipart requests) is regenerated. Any of these break the digest comparison in XML-DSig verification because Exclusive-C14N normalizes canonicalization-neutral formatting but does NOT paper over actual infoset differences (attribute reordering vs. original), and it certainly does not re-serialize equivalently to SAAJ's writer. Fix: intercept the raw HTTP body at Phase.RECEIVE (before any SAAJ touch), cache it via CachedOutputStream, stash it on the Exchange, and reset a fresh InputStream so downstream SAAJ still gets its bytes. Provider then reads back via wsContext.getMessageContext().get(RAW_XML_PAYLOAD) which — CONFIRMED both by CXF 4.1.8 bytecode analysis and by a live JVM test — delegates from the Message-map to the Exchange when the key isn't on the Message. Fallback to soapToString() remains for edge cases (e.g. non-HTTP transports without an InputStream). Verified working via 4 unit tests + module compile.
